div.head: NEW BOOKS, &c.
div.p: NEW BOOKS, &c.

1 A complete edition is published by Mr. Elliott , Scott, London, of the poems of William Leighton, illustrated by John Leighton. The author of this promising and interesting volume of poems resided for a greater part of his time in Liverpool,where he was highly esteemed by a large circle of admiring friends. He was stricketl down with typhoid fever, and died at the age of twenty-eight.. He was a nephew of Mr. Robert Leighton.. author of "'Records, and other poems" which, met with wide appreciation both in this country and in America. It will be seen, therefore, that he came of a poetical family, and bad he lived there can be no question than he would have taken a front, ranltatmongst the poets of this generation. His verse letender, grace- ful,.and melodious, and it is noticeabbe that his style grew in strength as he grew in years. The volume is accompanied with a portrait of the author, and it should be said of the illustrations that they are thoroughly artistic and finished prodactions. The work is one which the lover ofgood verse will appreciate. Whittaker's Almanac for 1890 is a• bulky volume of ever-700 closely printed pages, and it seems necessary to add to the bulk year by year. The supplementary ardbles include papers on the Administration of India under the Crown, the French Revolution, Submarine Navigation, the Irish Constabulary, Sec. But " Whit- taker " may be said to contain everything relating to the Government, finances, population,, commerce, and general statistics of the British Empire, with notices, by no,means inconsiderable, of other countries. The work, indeed, contains so much that it is difficult to say what it does not contain, for even those who are familiar with its pages are not unfrequently surprised to discover just the kind of information for which they may have been searching in other quarters. The Almanac is edited by ' Mr. Joseph Whittaker, F.S.A., who, must be tongratu- lated this, as other years, upon the admirable way in which he has accomplished his wonderful task. " John Bull and his other Island." is the title ef a shilling issue in paper covers, by Mr. Arthur Bennett, issued by the Sunrise Publishing Company. The " Other /Pland," it is hardly necessary to•state,.is Ireland, and the book is described in the preface as " a record of three holidays in that realm of mingled beauty and mis- fortune." Mr. Bennett is a fluent and tasteful writer, and when he keeps to purely descriptive writing, he is all that can be desired. He iSs. however, a strong opponent of Home Rule to Ireland, and what we cannot hut regard as a deep prejudice runs through well-nigh everything he has to say uponthe subject. What can be more absurd, for instance, than to•say " By a change unequalled in a career of kaleidiscopitall transformations, Mr. Gladstone had suddenly gone. over to the cause which, until the close of 1885.. he had persistently denounced." And again, M. Gladstone is "the prince of quacks, the king of conjurers, the paragon of whirli- gigs." 111 r. Bennett does not really mean what he says. We don't suppose he attaches an particular meaning to these phrases, but they tickle his fancy. They are a hit at Mr. Gladstone,and he therefore makes use of them. Apart from the organic' defect which We have noticed, the volume is written in a readable, style, and contains a considerable amount of information as to the districts visited by the author. "Everybody's Book of Proverbs and Quetations" is a capital little sixpenny volame of 160 pages, in cloth covers. The proverbs, &c., have been collected from all quarters, and classified by Mr. W. H. Howe. The book is published by Messrs. Howe and Co., London. The issue has already reached the 26th thousand, and it is likely to become more popular.. The Century" Magazine for April has for frontispiece a charming re-production of the "Madonna and child," by Giovanni Bethel. The interesting biogiaphy of Joseph Jefferson, the actor, is continued, and amongst other strikingly illustrated papers we have "The slave trade in the Congo Basin," "An artist's letter from Japan," "The Serpent Mound of Ohio," "The Old Poetic Guild in Ireland," " A Dusky Genius," and the " Shosskone Falls,' Bcc. " Scribner's "is also particularly strong in the current issne. The second part appears of. "In the footprints of Charles Lamb," by B. E. Martin. It is capitally written and charmingly illustrated. Amongst other noteworthy illustrated articles should be named—" Tadmore in the Wilderness," "The Electric Railway of To-day," "Expiation," by Octave Thant. and" In the Valley," by Harold Frederic: " The Police Minister "is a shilling novel published by Messrs. F. Warne and Co. It is from the pen of Mr. J. S. Borlase, who has had, a large experience in thisl class of writing, and is exceedingly skilful in working out a plot and filling it with interesting detail. " Thel Police Minister" is a startling story of life in Russia, and shows what a woman may become who is both Princess and Police Spy. " Lippincott's " for April contains as the leading com- plete story" A cast for fortune," by Christian Reid. Mr. Julian Hawthorn continues his papers on his father'sl " Elixir of Life,"•Mr. Wilson Barrett supplies a most thoughtful paper on" Hamlet," Dr. Green has an article on "Stanley's Emin Pasha Expedition," Mr. G. T. Betteney Writes on" The spirituality of marriage," and there are, besides, several other papers. The frontispiece to the "English Illustrated Magatine" is an engraving of the drawing" At the Ferry, by A. D. McCorinitk. Lord Lytton continues his romance "Ring of Amasia," and there is a paper, illustrated, on "Rowing at Oxford and Cambridge," and other interest- ing articles, illustrated, are "-Social life in Bulgaria,"] and" A glimpse of Highclere Castle." ' The " Manchester Quarterly," published for the Man- chester Literary Club by Mr. John Heywood, has for frontispiece a capital portrait of the late Robert Brown- ing', followed by thotightful and critical papers on " Some aspects of Browning," by J. Milner, C. E. Tyrer, and J. Mortimer. Mr. A. Edmeston.contributea a poem on" Autumn Reverie," and the rest of the contents in- clude" The philosophy in Lever's Barrington," "Leisure and Modern Life," "They had been friends in youth," "Concerning nature and some of her lovers," and" W. Flazlitt." The Newbery - House Magazine (Messrs. Griffith Farrell and Co.), continues strong and varied. In this month's issue Judge Cox discourses on " Tithes," Capon Benhem revives" Some Easter memories," Mr. David !ter eimotks a racy paper on "A Itornan Camp in the Afrca.n Deserts_," Miss Gibcrne • writes on "The Little Folks of Art Land," and there are other interesting pacers, stories, dm. Weldoe'. Ladies' Journal for April, in addition to use- ful notes, kc., contains coloured plate, cut-out pattern of a vralkleg skirt, lessons in millinery, Sc.c.•

THE RENOVATION.

This place of worship which has been closed for the past ten weeks will be re-opened to-morrow (Sunclay), after having undergone a complete renovation and decoration. Its internal appear- ance has been greatly improved by the work which has been completed. and attractive designs executed in rich and admirably blending colours refldcts the highest credit upon those who have been entrested with. the work. The whole of the decoration has been carried out from original and elaborate designs by Mr:. George Faulkner Armitage, of Altrincharn, a brother of Mr. Z. Armitage, who is the organist and one of the deacons of the church. Mr., F. Armitage's services have been gratuitous, and the really beautiful results which have been obtained are ample evidence of their value. The decoration of the ceiling consists of diaper work in vermilion and brown, each panel ; being bordered with a plain, cool drab colour. The cornices dividing the centre of the ceiling from the portions over the galleries are in separate tones interspersed with stencil work. The ceiling over the galleries is a plain vellum tone, which has the effect of show- ing off to the best advantage, the fine work, over the body of the church. The upper part of the waifs has been fawn-tinted, while between the window spaces are striking artistic designs, which have received special treatment in yellow and maroon. The windows are bordered with fine. stencil work of a new and attractive design.. There has been almost a complete transferm- ation in the appearance of the organ cham- ber. The decoration has been carried out with a view to secure an, effect corresponding with that in the body of the church. A dado of stencil work, walls level with the front galleries; tm mentioned that the instrument, , ranundsit along should itself has bedn thoroughly repaired, cleaned t and decorated. The washing of the gold on the pips has brought out an effective glitter which is . in striking contrast to the colours in which the pipes, have been treated. The dgccration of the pillars, consist of dark blue and light blue bands from: about three feet off the ground to the bead pieces: The lower portion of the pillars is bedecked with stencil work and red bands, while the capitals have, all been repainted: and re-decorated. The gas pen-- , dents have been similarly treated—the prominent ! colours used being gold, blue, and brown. The. 'roof of the vestibule has been decorated in accord-. ance with Mr. Armitage's original designs,each panel being occupied by elaborate stencil work: The wall of the vestibule are diapered, with an effective dado, of stencil work five feet from the ground. A,new feature of the decorations in the vestibule has been, the addition of scriptural texts—near the ceiling. On the wall dividing the church and the vestibule appears, the text "I dwell in a high and holy; place witAh Him also those of a contrite and humble spitit." To the left is the further quotation " If God be forus„ who can be against us," while at the opposite end are the words "God is our refuge, and our strength'' In addition to the painting and decoration) the whole of the woodwork of the church has been cleaned and re-varnished. The painting decoration, has been remarkably well:carried out by Messrs. T. Hesketh and Sons,.of Warrington. Messrs. R. Garnett and Son have supplied new carpets: cocoa-nut. matting has been obtained', from Mr. Mounfield ; and the organ has been repaired and retuned by Messrs. Richardson, of Manchester. The total estimated cost of the work is 2420: to- wards which amount over £3OO have, been proinised

About an acre of cultivated land on the, verge of Sheppey Cliff, Sheerness, fell into the sea, on Wednesday, shortly after the' occupier had passed over al The Rev. J. Ossian Davies, of Bournemouth, formerly Congregational minister at 'follington Park, ndon, has it is said, been selected as Liberal candidate for East Carmarthenshire at the next general election. The police entered the Pidelio Club, i*Greek-street, Lcndon, on Wednesday, and made fiftrseven arrests. Money, a faretable, and some cards were,seized. Later the defendants were charged with frequenting a betting house. Probate of the will of the late Mr. Talbst, M.P., has ! been granted to the sole executrix, his daughter, the gross value of the personal estate being sworn at £1,388,817 13s. Evictions on the Ponsonby Estates were resumed on Wednesday morning by Sheriff Gaie..end up to noon six families had become dispossessed. There was no resist- ance; and very little excitement.,

You can do it in your spare moments. To every one who counts the correct number of E's in St. John's Gospel,' use the old version Bible as found in every home, not the revised edition, will ne presented with a Diamond Cluster Ring. Here is the secret Having entered into an arrangement with a world-renowned firm of wholesale jewellers, and as I always purchase largely for cash, thus obtaining large discounts. I can supply gold and silver jewellery of every description at from 40 to 50 per cent. cheaper than any retail house ; and by this advertisement I seek to get in direct communication with, and to place spec... mens of my jewellery in the hands, of every reader of this paper, and thus for every article so given away I shall be en- abled to sell ten. TO THE BURGESSES OF THE NORTH-WEST WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, Having been requested by representatives of all sections of the Burgesses in the Ward to become a candidate for the seat in the Council, rendered vacant by the lamented death of Mr. John Greening. I have consented to place my services at your disposal. For many years I have taken a deep interest in all political and municipal matters. The course of recent events in the Council, relating to the Extension of tile Borough, the Sanitation, and the general Improvement, has been, and will be, watched by me most carefully. I have long been in favor of the Freeing of the Library, and am pleased to see there is now a prospect of its early accom- plishment. The question of the purchase of the Waterworks is most Important to all the ratepayers, and I shall give to it my thoughtful consideration. As a member of one of the most numerous and important sections of the community, viz., the working classes, I shall, owing to my acqnaintance with our wants, be the better able to keep a watchful eye upon all efforts to improve our dwell- ings, and increase the comfort of our homes. I shall also watch, so far as I can, the general expenditure of the Borough, being assured that efficiency and economy can be made to go hand in hand. jam. Ladiee and Gentlemen, Your obedient Servant, SAM. J, 13EAMAN. 96, Bewsey Road, April 11th, 1890. '

BOROUGH OF WARRINGTON. MUNICIPAL ELECTION. NORTH-WEST WARD. TO THE BURGESSES OF THE WARD. LLDIFS AND GENTLEMEN, Having been urgently requested by a large and influen- tial body of the Ratepayers of the Ward to become a candi- date for election, as your representative in the Town Connell, in place of the late Councillor Greening, I have con- sented to'do so, and if elected my constant object will be to do all in my power for the improvement of the town and its trade, thus creating and improving labour and wages for the working-classes, and business for the shdpkeepers and com- mercial interest. I will also give my best attention to the Improvement of the Streets, Gas Service, and Sanitary Ar- rangements, as well as to full efficiency, with due economy in all matters connected with the Ward and Borough. As one who has always taken a deep and active interest in the Institutions of the Borough, and in everything calculated to promote the general welfare and prosperity of my fellow townsmen, added to the long period I have lived among you. I feel that I may appeal with confidence to my fellow workingmen and many good friends for their assistance in this contest, and to the Burgesses of the Ward for their votes on the day of the Poll. I am, Ladies and Gentlemen, Your Obedient Servant, JOHN ROBERTS. Warrington, April 12th, 1890.

TWENTY THOUSAND ACRES AMERICAN PRO- PERTY FREE. In allotments of Farm, Fruit, and Vineyard Tracts of 40, 20:10, and 5 acres each, and selected Residence or Business Lots. ONE of the above divisions of Real Estate Pro- perty, located either in the Golden State of fruitful California, or in the famous Orangegrove State of Florida, will be unconditionally given free from any charge for the land to any respectable person who sends his or her full name and post address to the American Office of the Californian and Southern Land Company at Cincinnati, Ohio, U.S.A. As soon as your name and address are received by the Com- pany, a free Land Warrant for one of the allotments of free property will be returned to you by first ocean post. The I only cost for the property will be an expense fee for executing a Warranty Transfer Title Deed in your favour, and having the signatures thereto legally acknowledged before the ptoper officials. Such expense will in no ease exceed 125., and is not to be paid until after you have received the Free Lend War- rant. When one or more members of the same family, or friends, wish to secure property together, the Company will issue to any applicant as many Free Land Warrants as may be requested, not to exceed ten, to be given by the applicant to those whom he applies for. The object in making this extraordinary offer Is to secure a diversified interest and ownership throughout the different countries of Europe in the lands owned and controlled by the above-named Company. When this is accomplished. the Company will open branch offices in various huropean Cities, and offer its large remaining properties for sale at a uniform price of £5 per acre for Farm and Fruit Tracts, and £6 per Plot for Residence or Business Lots. It is believed by the Company that the diversified interest that will be thus secured by this preliminary method of advertising will amply compensate for the amount of pro- perty that is now offered FREE. If the number of names sent for free property is in excess of the amount of such property, those whose names are re- ceived first will secure I. Hence the advantage of sending name and address at once. All that need be sent is an envelope bearing your name and post address ; this envelope to be enclosed in another and the outer envelope to be addressed as follows: THE CALIFORNIA AND SOUTHERN LAND CO., CINCINNATI, OHIO, U.S.A. NOTE.--If preferred, application may be made to the Com- pany's Branch Office in London. A penny stamped self- addressed envelope sent to the Company's London Agent, Mr. 1 W. 11. FULLER, 8, College Chambers. High Holborn. Lon- don, will secure a FREE LAND WARRANT, issued by the I Home Company, the same as if sent direct to the Dead Office.
